brand.name: Riverkeepers Trust
brand.descriptor: A local charity that cleans, restores and watches over the rivers of the Wye valley with volunteers.

text.heading: Our rivers are choking. Volunteers are bringing them back.
text.body: Farm run-off and plastic have turned stretches of the Wye and its streams green and still. Every weekend, local people pull out rubbish, plant banks and test the water.

text.heading: Why we exist
text.body: We believe a river belongs to everyone who lives along it, and that the people who live along it are the ones best placed to look after it. We train volunteers, restore riverbanks and publish what the water tests show, so the whole valley can see what is changing.

text.heading: What we do
text.body: Three programmes, all run by volunteers with a small staff team behind them.

items.title: Clean-ups
items.body: Monthly work days that clear rubbish and invasive weeds from the banks.

items.title: Bank planting
items.body: Native trees and reeds that hold the soil and shade the water.

items.title: Citizen testing
items.body: Trained volunteers sample the water each week and publish the results.

text.heading: Last year on the river
text.body: Figures from our annual report, counted by volunteers and checked by our staff.

items.quote: I came for one Saturday clean-up. Three years later I run the testing team for our stretch.
items.name: Delyth Morgan

items.quote: The kingfishers came back to the bend below our farm the second summer after the planting.
items.name: Gareth Pryce

text.heading: Where your money goes
text.body: We publish our accounts and our water results every year.

items.fact: Registered charity number 1180000 in England and Wales
82 pence in every pound goes straight to river work

items.title: Autumn clean-up at Glasbury
items.body: Bring boots and gloves; we bring the grabbers, bags and tea.

items.title: Water testing training
items.body: An evening session for new testers in Builth Wells.

items.title: Tree planting day
items.body: Four hundred alders and willows along the Ithon.

text.heading: Give to the river
text.body: A one-off gift pays for a clean-up day. A monthly gift keeps testing going all year.

items.name: One-off gift
items.impact: Buys grabbers and bags for a clean-up team of ten.

items.name: Monthly gift
items.impact: Covers a year of test kits for one volunteer tester.

text.heading: Give a Saturday to the river
text.body: No experience needed. We train you, lend you the kit and pair you with someone who knows the stretch.

text.tagline: Volunteers restoring the rivers of the Wye valley.
